skills.title: Cache address fields
skills.subject: Computer Organization
skills.principle: Convert capacity and block size to the same addressable unit. Sets = capacity / (block size × ways). Offset = log2(block size); index = log2(sets); tag = address width − index − offset.
skills.contrast: Changing associativity changes the number of sets, even when capacity and block size stay fixed.

probes.prompt: A byte-addressed machine has 32-bit addresses, a 16 KiB direct-mapped cache and 32-byte blocks. How many tag bits are needed? (1 KiB = 1024 bytes.)
probes.explanation: There are 512 lines: 9 index bits and 5 offset bits. The tag is 32 − 9 − 5 = 18 bits.

probes.prompt: The same byte-addressed machine now uses a 4-way cache. Capacity remains 16 KiB and each block is still 32 bytes. How many tag bits are needed?
probes.explanation: There are 128 sets: 7 index bits and 5 offset bits. The tag is 32 − 7 − 5 = 20 bits.

skills.title: Page replacement decisions
skills.subject: Operating Systems
skills.principle: Count a fault whenever the referenced page is absent, including initial loads. FIFO updates arrival order only on insertion; LRU updates recency on every reference. Optimal replacement uses the next future use.
skills.contrast: A hit changes recency for LRU but does not change arrival order for FIFO.

probes.prompt: Two frames are initially empty. For references 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, how many page faults occur under FIFO?
probes.explanation: The first two references fault. The hit on 1 does not move it in FIFO order. Loading 3 evicts 1, so the last reference faults again: 4 faults.

probes.prompt: Two frames are initially empty. For the same references 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, how many page faults occur under LRU?
probes.explanation: The hit on 1 makes 2 least recently used. Loading 3 evicts 2, and the final 1 is a hit: 3 faults.

skills.title: Sliding-window limits
skills.subject: Computer Network
skills.principle: With n sequence bits, standard Go-Back-N uses a receiver window of 1 and sender window at most 2^n − 1. Equal sender/receiver windows in Selective Repeat are at most 2^(n−1). For a lossless link with negligible ACK transmission and processing, utilization is min(1, W / (1 + 2Tp/Tt)).
skills.contrast: The same sequence space supports different window limits when the receiver accepts out-of-order frames.

probes.prompt: A standard Go-Back-N protocol uses 3-bit frame sequence numbers and a receiver window of 1. What is the largest safe sender window, in frames?
probes.explanation: The sequence space has 8 values. Go-Back-N needs one value outside the sender window, giving a maximum of 7.

probes.prompt: A standard Selective Repeat protocol uses the same 3-bit sequence numbers, with equal sender and receiver window sizes. What is the largest safe window, in frames?
probes.explanation: Old and new receive windows must not overlap after wraparound. Twice the window must fit in the 8-value space, so the maximum is 4.
